scenario: AITA. Gave my cousin a gift, his parents tried to take it away as punishment for something I think is unfair and I told them to give it back to me? | I’m 21F, and my 2 cousins are 15M(Tj) and 13M(Ked). When the newest iPhones launched, I gifted Tj and Ked 1 each. Turns out Ked has been stealing money from some extended family members, Ked himself admitted to this. A fight broke out and Keds parents defended him, didn’t care he was stealing money and cut the extended family members off. Over winter break, Ked apologized to extended family and made amends, but his parents are stubborn and narcissistic and will never admit they’re wrong and just basically hates extended family now. The extended family members hosted a house warming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to come but their parents told Ked they didn’t want him to go Incase extended family tried accusing him of stealing again, and told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and they trusted him to make the right decision. Ked stayed home and Tj came to the sleep over/housewarming. Cue his phone blowing up with his parents yelling at him for coming to extended families house. How he’s a disappointment. They trusted him to make the right decision and he failed. How if they hate someone he needs to follow along and hate them too. I saw all these texts and can confirm 100% they said this. Tj asked to be left out of the drama and they repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for 2 weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he NEVER got punished. I’m sorry but I just don’t agree, I’m completely disgusted by the way they raise their kids and have just lost all respect for the parents. I told them while I can’t control how they discipline their children, it’s not their property to take away from him, and I won’t go behind their back and let him use the phone but since it was my gift to him, I’d like to hold on to it until the 2 weeks are up. Welp, of course the narcissistic parents made a big deal and other extended family members are telling me I should’ve just stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want and I’m only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they’re treating him unfairly. We all can agree they’re horrible parents. If they were decent parents and was punishing him for something fair, I WOULDNT have asked for the phone back. Heres where I may be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules, so I decided to take some of their “power” away by asking for my gift back.

Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, I'm 21, and my cousins are 15 and 13. I bought them new iPhones when they were launched. Now, one of them, Ked, has been stealing money from extended family members. He admitted to it, but his parents didn't care and even defended him. They cut off the extended family members. Then, during winter break, Ked apologized and made amends, but his parents are still stubborn and narcissistic, hating the extended family. The extended family hosted a housewarming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to come, but their parents told Ked he couldn't go in case the extended family accused him of stealing again. They told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and trusted him to make the right decision. Ked stayed home, and Tj came to the sleepover. Then, Tj's phone started blowing up with his parents yelling at him for coming to the extended family's house. They were really upset and said he failed because they trusted him to make the right decision. They also said if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When Tj came back home, they grounded him and took his phone away for two weeks. Ked admitted to stealing but never got punished. I'm really upset about how they're raising their kids and have lost all respect for the parents. I told them that while I can't control how they discipline their children, it's not their property to take away from him. I don't want to go behind their backs and let him use the phone, but since it was my gift to him, I want to hold onto it until the two weeks are up. Of course, the narcissistic parents made a big deal out of it, and other extended family members are telling me I should have stayed out of it and let them raise their kid how they want. I'm only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they're treating him unfairly. Here's where I might be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules. So, I decided to take some of their power away by asking for my gift back. Now, I need to figure out if this is right or wrong. Let me think about the different aspects. First, the phone was my gift to Tj. Legally, it's mine, so I have the right to ask for it back. But morally, is it fair to take it back because I disagree with how his parents are treating him? On one hand, I'm standing up for Tj and trying to protect him from unfair treatment. On the other hand, I'm interfering in how his parents are raising him, which could be seen as overstepping. I also need to consider the impact on Tj. If I take the phone back, does that help him or make things worse? He might feel supported by me, but his parents might react negatively, making the situation more tense. Another thing to think about is the precedent this sets. If I take the phone back now, what does that mean for future situations? Will I always feel the need to intervene when I think something is unfair? I also need to reflect on why I'm so upset. Is it because I care about Tj, or is there another reason? Understanding my own motivations can help me make a more objective decision. Maybe I should talk to Tj directly and see how he feels about the situation. Does he want me to take the phone back, or does he prefer to handle it with his parents? Also, considering the advice from other extended family members, they think I should stay out of it. Is there any merit to their perspective? Perhaps they believe in letting parents raise their children without interference. But I also have to weigh that against my concern for Tj's well-being. If I think his parents are treating him unfairly, is it my responsibility to step in? I should also think about the bigger picture. How does this situation affect our family relationships? Could my actions lead to more conflict or help resolve it? In the end, I need to decide whether asking for the phone back is the right thing to do, considering all these factors.
